prompt: In the two-way branching algorithm for Vertex Cover, every choice consumes one unit of cover budget. What changes when the graph grows but that budget stays fixed?

options.text: The search-tree size is still controlled by the fixed budget, while edge-processing work grows
options.explanation: This is the FPT separation: a parameter-only search factor times polynomial graph work.

options.text: The running time becomes independent of the graph
options.explanation: Every recursion node still inspects or filters edges.

options.text: The recursion depth grows with the number of vertices regardless of budget
options.explanation: Each branch reduces the budget, which bounds depth.

options.text: FPT guarantees a practical runtime for every budget
options.explanation: The parameter factor can be huge; fixed-parameter tractability is a growth classification.

workedExample: Every branch consumes one unit of cover budget and there are two possible endpoints to choose. The search tree is bounded by that budget, while each node processes the current graph. Increasing graph size at a fixed budget keeps only polynomial growth; increasing the budget can cause a much sharper rise. Fixed-parameter tractability is not independence from graph size.
